summary: Backend-only regression after requirements.txt trim. Verified installed runtime deps match trimmed file, backend RUNNING in supervisor with no ImportError/ModuleNotFound in logs, and full pytest suite (18 tests) passes 100%: /api/health, /api/, /api/openapi.json, POST /api/leads (all 6 services, UUID id, status=new, ISO created_at), validation 422s (empty/whitespace name, short phone, invalid service), GET /api/leads auth (401 no/wrong token, 200 with X-Admin-Token, sorted newest-first, no _id leak), PATCH /api/leads/{id} (401s, 404 unknown id, new<->processed toggle, 422 invalid status). Confirmed Mongo persistence directly via motor and that VK notification is silently skipped with VK_TOKEN/VK_PEER_ID unset (lead creation still 201). Also re-verified `pip install --dry-run --index-url https://pypi.org/simple -r requirements.txt` resolves cleanly from public PyPI, and `import server` + `import httpx/motor` work. Light frontend smoke: GET / => 200, GET /admin => 200.
critical_code_review_comments: requirements.txt has no transitive gaps: starlette/anyio/h11 arrive via fastapi/uvicorn/httpx; dnspython via pymongo. Note motor 3.3.1 pins pymongo>=4.5,<5 so the explicit pymongo==4.6.3 pin is compatible but must be kept in sync on future motor upgrades.

For production Docker, consider adding a `uvicorn[standard]` extra or explicit gunicorn/worker choice if the client's deployment expects websockets/http-tools; plain uvicorn==0.25.0 is fine for the current REST-only API.
pytest/requests are prod-image bloat; consider a separate requirements-dev.txt so the client's VPS image stays minimal (non-blocking).
seed_data_creation: Created TEST_-prefixed leads during the run; all 38 TEST_ leads deleted afterwards (5 pre-existing non-TEST leads left untouched).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Test suite is xdist-parallel (pytest.ini uses -n --dist loadscope); do NOT rely on module-level shared lists across tests. I replaced the shared created_lead_ids dependency in TestPatchLead with a class-scoped own_lead_id fixture that creates its own lead — the two previous failures were purely this xdist state issue, not product bugs. Also added test_health. Run with: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/backend_test.py -v (no extra -p flags, pytest.ini already sets xdist args).
rca_of_the_issue: Initial 2 failures (TestPatchLead toggle/invalid-status) were caused by pytest-xdist distributing classes to separate workers, leaving the module-global created_lead_ids empty in the worker running TestPatchLead. Fixed in test code with a class-scoped fixture that creates its own lead. No application regression from the requirements.txt trim was found.
